$comment: Shared configuration for the tscircuit workspace. Read by ./tsc-dev; this is the single source of truth for what MAP.md documents in prose. Plain JSON (not JSONC) so `node -e` can read it with no dependency; explanatory text lives in `description` fields, which the tooling prints, rather than in comments nothing can see.

runtime.description: The packages that turn React/TSX into a rendered board — the 'system'. See `bundling` below before rebuilding any of these.

viewers.description: React components / libs that render Circuit JSON.

exporters.description: Circuit JSON to manufacturing / interchange formats.

autorouting.description: Trace routing: the main MIT autorouter plus the solvers it is built from.

solvers.description: Standalone 2D algorithms, each with its own Cosmos debugger (`bun run start`).

formats.description: The data format and the parsers/DSLs around it.

importers.description: Foreign formats into Circuit JSON / tscircuit source.

bundling.description: Which packages are baked into which other packages at BUILD time. tscircuit packages are inlined, not resolved from node_modules at runtime: core/props/circuit-json are bundled into eval's webworker, that worker is base64-embedded into runframe's standalone.min.js, and the cli serves that bundle. So a change is invisible downstream until every level below it is rebuilt, bottom-up — `./tsc-dev rebuild --from <repo>` computes that order from this graph. Read each entry as 'consumer: packages baked into it'. The graph is advisory and deliberately a superset of literal inlining (rebuilding one level too many is harmless; one level too few silently ships a stale bundle) — edges are verified against the consumer's real package.json at run time, and edges to repos you have not cloned are skipped.

parametric-enclosures.description: Repos carrying the parametric-enclosure patch set, in release order (see create-fdm-enclosure/README.md). Downstream rebuild-only repos (eval, runframe, cli) are excluded — they carry no patch branch. Override the effort with SYNC_FORK_EFFORT, or one branch for every repo with SYNC_FORK_BRANCH.
